source: Hand-curated limits on the ICAO aerodrome code (A-F) of stands whose OpenStreetMap spacing misjudges their size: the import derives a code from the distance to the nearest mapped stand, then a rule with the longest matching stand-name prefix raises it to at_least and caps it at at_most. No airport publishes a stand table openly; EDDK and EDDP use the VATSIM Germany knowledge base (unofficial, flight-simulation community: 'EDDK Ground', knowledgebase.vatsim-germany.org/books/sops-fir-langen/page/eddk-ground, and 'EDDP - Leipzig/Halle', knowledgebase.vatsim-germany.org/books/airports-munchen-fir-edmm/page/eddp-leipzighalle, read November 2026; for EDDP its per-bay wingspan limits of the DHL hub apron). Terminal piers A-D carry no published size there; they serve A320 and B737 jets daily, so code C is a lower bound estimated from the airlines' fleets.

rules.note: Terminal 1 (piers A-C) and Terminal 2 (pier D) contact and apron stands: estimate from the A320/B737 fleets of Eurowings, Ryanair and the leisure carriers; VATSIM names D51 as a code C stand
Cargo aprons E and F: 'most of the heavy lifting cargo fleet (e.g. B747)' (VATSIM Germany)
A380 positions, primary E31, E33, E35, E41, E45 and secondary E43, F21, F23, F25, F31 (VATSIM Germany)
Cargo feeder apron W: 'B737, ATR and B757/B767' (VATSIM Germany)
Apron V: cargo feeders up to B757/B767 and business aviation 'up to B737-BBJ' depending on the position (VATSIM Germany); the spacing decides which
Apron 1 airline stands 101-111 (non-jetway) and 126-136 (jetway) per VATSIM Germany; code C at least is an estimate from the A320/B737 airline fleets
DHL hub apron 4, A-Bay 401-412: 'max. 52 m' wingspan (VATSIM Germany, EDDP page)
DHL hub apron 4, B-Bay 421-436: 'max. 36 m' (VATSIM Germany)

DHL hub apron 4, D-Bay L/R positions: 'max. 36 m' (VATSIM Germany)
